title: Orientation + Alif & the ب ت ث family
objectives: Explain that Arabic is read right-to-left and letters are learned by shape-family
Identify and correctly pronounce ا ب ت ث in isolation, on sight, in random order
Locate the makhraj (articulation point) for each of these 4 letters when asked

slides.heading: How this course works
body: Live lesson + this slide deck + tap-to-hear + daily homework
Three lessons a week (Mon/Wed/Sat), 15–20 min practice every day
Nothing is ever locked — repeat any lesson, any time

slides.heading: Arabic reads right-to-left
body: Lines flow right → left; so do the letters inside a word
We learn letters in shape-families (letters that look alike), not dictionary order

slides.heading: Makhraj — where a sound is born
body: Every Arabic letter has one home in your mouth or throat
Five broad zones: chest cavity, throat, tongue, lips, nose
Getting the makhraj right IS tajweed's foundation — we start today, not in Phase 3

audio.title: Muallimi Soniy — the letters that make A, I, U

slides.makhraj: al-jawf — the empty space of the mouth/chest cavity; an open, unobstructed sound
notes: The simplest letter: a single vertical stroke
In Phase 2 alif becomes the long-vowel (madd) letter — foreshadow only

audio.cue: ب: both lips close fully, then release — like English b but with complete lip contact
ت: tongue-tip taps the ridge behind the upper front teeth — light, no heaviness

slides.makhraj: tip of tongue against the upper front teeth / gum ridge
notes: Two dots ABOVE the body — same body as ب

audio.cue: ث: tongue-tip BETWEEN the teeth, unvoiced 'th' as in think — never plain t, never s

slides.makhraj: tip of tongue between the teeth (interdental)
notes: Three dots ABOVE — same body as ب and ت

slides.heading: Spot the dots
slides.instructions: Same body, different dots. Teacher points, student names the letter and its dot pattern.

slides.heading: Name it back
slides.instructions: Teacher says a letter name aloud; student points to it and says it back. All 4 letters, randomized, 3 rounds.

slides.heading: 28 or 29 letters?
body: You may hear both numbers. Hamza (ء) is a glottal-stop mark — in this course we count 28 letters and treat hamza separately when it appears.
1-minute aside — details in the linked video, optional

slides.heading: Homework — 15–20 min/day
tasks: Print the flashcard sheet from the practice page (ا ب ت ث, one per box)
Say each letter's name + sound aloud 10× per letter in mixed order — tick the tally boxes
Re-watch the two linked Arabic101 orientation videos once this week

drills.title: Flashcard grid
drills.instructions: Name each letter + produce its sound. Shuffle your order every round.

audio.cue: ب: both lips close fully, then release
ت: tongue-tip taps behind upper front teeth
ث: tongue between teeth, soft 'th' as in think

drills.title: Minimal-pair listening: ت vs ث
drills.instructions: Someone says ت or ث — point to the glyph you heard. (With your teacher live, or self-test against the cue lines.)

audio.cue: plain t — tongue on gum ridge

dailyChecklist: Watch one linked orientation video (first two days)

script: Open with the course tour (slide 2): live lessons Mon/Wed/Sat, slides re-openable at home, tap-to-hear on every Arabic item, nothing is ever locked.
Makhraj slide: keep it plain-English — 'where the sound is born'. Do not introduce Arabic zone names yet.
Model each letter's sound 3× before asking the student to imitate; correct on the FIRST wrong repetition, not the third (ijazah-style immediate correction — teaching-mistakes-assessment.md B).
Before the lesson: self-check your own ث and ب against the linked Arabic101 orientation videos — teacher voice is the student's primary audio for these letters.
listenFor: ث flattened toward plain ت or toward س — Uzbek/Turkic phonology has no interdental fricative; highest-risk error of the lesson
ب produced without full lip closure (weak v-like glide)
ا given an added glottal catch (hamza) — isolated alif should be open and unobstructed
teacherNotes.homework: Flashcard sheet ا ب ت ث, 10× per letter daily in mixed order with tally boxes; re-watch both orientation videos once.
